dedupe_keys.name: rapid group effects on pile downdrag following liquefaction

description: RAPID: Group Effects on Pile Downdrag Following Liquefaction is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Richard Coffman, University of Arkansas Fayetteville (uark.edu). The New Madrid Seismic Zone (NMSZ), located within the Mississippi Embayment, has produced large earthquakes with detrimental effects due to deep soil deposits and resulting high peak horizontal ground accelerations. The alluvial soil deposits within the Mississippi Embayment include loose sands that are located below the ground water table; these sands are susceptible to liquefaction. Coverage: Blytheville, Arkansas, USA. DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Pile Driving Analyzer, Blast Induced Liquefaction. Published 2024-05-08. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
